title: Where Wilt Thou Go Since Night Draws Near
description: Where Wilt Thou Go Since Night Draws Near in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Ernst Christoph Homburg wrote these words in German. August Crull's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 227.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Where wilt Thou go since night draws near, O Je-sus Christ, Thou Pil-grim dear? Lord, make me hap-py, be my Guest, And in my heart, oh, deign to rest.

lines: Where wilt Thou go since night draws near,
O Jesus Christ, Thou Pilgrim dear?
Lord, make me happy, be my Guest,
And in my heart, oh, deign to rest.
Grant my request, O dearest Friend,
For truly I Thy best intend;
Thou knowest that Thou ever art
A welcome Guest unto my heart.
The day is now far spent and gone,
The shades of night come quickly on;
Then stay with me, Thou heavenly Light,
And do not leave me in this night.
Enlighten me that from the way
That leads to heaven I may not stray,
That I may never be misled,
Though night of sin is round me spread.
And when I on my death-bed lie,
Help me and let me gently die.
Abide! I will not let Thee go!
Thou wilt not leave me, Lord, I know.

licence: Public domain: Ernst Christoph Homburg died in 1681; August Crull died in 1923.
credits: Words by Ernst Christoph Homburg (1605–1681), translated by August Crull (1845–1923), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
